rows.measured_conditions: bulk polycrystalline textured fcc NiH with octahedral H; hot-extracted H/Ni = 1.05 +/- 0.05
rows.band_observation_not_loss: main band peak at 89 meV, with high-energy shoulder to about 130 meV; 89 meV is the peak energy, not an FWHM, HWHM or lifetime
rows.reason: The reported first-band position, spread and instrument resolution cannot determine a homogeneous single-mode linewidth or lifetime. Peak and shoulder combine q/mode dispersion and the paper does not supply a separated lifetime.

rows.band_observation_not_loss: Gaussian peak position 55.8 meV with Gaussian FWHM 4.8 meV, fitted as one component of a three-Gaussian band

lifetime_bound.kind: conditional width-as-ceiling ONLY, not established by the source
lifetime_bound.assumption: Only IF selected-mode homogeneous Lorentzian FWHM is <= fitted PdH Gaussian-band-component4.8meV. The source does not establish this identification or a universal mode-wise bound. No numeric NiH/PdD lifetime bound follows from quoted energies/resolution.
lifetime_bound.relation: Gamma2=1/T2=1/(2T1)+gamma_pure, gamma_pure>=0; threshold assumes the same simple Markov oscillator projection.

rows.reason: 4.8 meV is a Gaussian band-fit FWHM, not a measured homogeneous Lorentzian FWHM. Phonon dispersion and instrument response are not disentangled; do not convert this raw band width to kappa.

rows.mode: accepted lattice cold small-amplitude Gamma reference
rows.source: V. E. Antonov et al., Phys. Rev. B 80, 134302 (2009), pp. 134302-1–4, Secs. II–III and Figs. 1–5: http://www.issp.ac.ru/lhpp/PapersAntonov/163.pdf
rows.measured_conditions: bulk fcc PdD(1-x)H(x), total (D+H)/Pd = 1.00 +/- 0.03; isotope fractions x = 0.050, 0.072, 0.091. The reported undisturbed-PdD spectrum is extracted from mixtures, not a direct isotopically pure PdD sample.
rows.band_observation_not_loss: first optic band has a maximum at 37 meV and a shoulder extending to about 65 meV; neither 37 meV nor the shoulder span is FWHM, HWHM or lifetime
rows.reason: The near-stoichiometric PdD matrix result is a q-integrated band, while the mode-resolved PdD0.63 line shape contains substantial nonstoichiometric structure; neither available source gives a matching isolated homogeneous loss value. Neither may be replaced by a PdH number.

rows.kind: exploratory bare code gamma=0.01, NOT measured
rows.mode: hybrid optic mode at q*d=pi/2; not the current lattice Gamma reference
rows.source: accepted pumps.json/rank.py/domain.py; gamma is a bare dimensionless viscous coefficient in time E0*t/hbar
rows.convention: lambda is the dimensionless canonical dynamical pole; kappa=-2 Re(lambda)*E0/hbar, Omega=Im(lambda)*E0/hbar. The input gamma is NOT kappa/Omega.

rows.kind: calculated, NOT measured; conditional on-shell Markov surrogate
rows.mode: PdH x=1,L optic4/5,295K; on-shell constant-self-energy surrogate, not a measured Lorentzian
rows.frequency_qualification: Approximate shifted branch in Fig2d, not the tabulated on-shell SSCHA reference; threshold approximate.
rows.transfer: Not a NiH/PdD measurement or a calibrated Gamma loss; multi-peak/frequency-dependent response can invalidate one Markov pole.

range_meaning: Two named scenarios, NOT confidence bounds or proved limits for actual material loss.
threshold: On resonance: h_eff=h_code*Omega_ref^2*P/Omega_q^2; h_eff,th=2*kappa/Omega_q; h_code,th=2*kappa*Omega_q/(Omega_ref^2*P). P is the mass-normalized pump-mode projection. At the lattice Gamma reference P=1 and h_code=h_eff.
hybrid_bare: For the earlier hybrid projection h_eff=delta_k/(M_dyn*nu^2), h_bare=delta_k/k_bare. They are not generally equal.
linewidth: Isolated homogeneous Lorentzian only: FWHM_E=2*hbar*Gamma2. Pure amplitude-friction case has Gamma2=kappa/2, T2=2/kappa and T1=1/kappa; extra pure dephasing prevents equating T1 and T2.
incident_reason: AC stiffness modulation is not an incident field. Transmission, mode-curvature coupling and accompanying DC shift are not supplied.
lookup: Bounded primary lookup complete; no qualifying measured homogeneous bulk optic loss established for any of the three materials.
